questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you must turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: How far your vehicle travels before stopping is affected by:

options.text: How fast your vehicle is traveling.
The condition of your brakes and tires.

questions.explanation: How far your vehicle travels before stopping depends on your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the pavement.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Make drivers angry about slow traffic.
Keep traffic out of dangerous work areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic out of dangerous work areas.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for workers and drivers. When you see cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests, slow down and follow their directions.

questions.question: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop when other drivers make sudden moves.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop when you need to react to other drivers' sudden movements.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing, you should:
questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing sign, slow down and look for a train. Be ready to stop. If the lights flash or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not try to go around the gate.

questions.question: If you have had several beers, the effects can only be reduced by:
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Cold showers, coffee, or exercise will not speed this up. It takes about one hour for your body to process one drink.

questions.question: You feel angry after an incident at work. When you get to your car, you should:

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the highway to let off steam.
Take a few minutes to calm down before you start driving home.
Stop at a bar and have a few drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before you start driving home.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, take time to calm down before driving. Driving angry is dangerous for you and others on the road.

questions.question: Before you start the engine, you should:

options.text: Make sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.

questions.explanation: Before you start the engine, buckle your safety belt and make sure all passengers buckle theirs too.

questions.question: Motor vehicle drivers should give extra space to children on bicycles because:

options.text: They do not react as quickly as adults.
They are smaller and harder to see than adults.

questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Be extra careful near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, and parks. Watch for children riding bikes on sidewalks — they may suddenly enter the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has a series of curves and turns.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol will help the medicine cure a cold.
The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.
There is no effect because they are different substances.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and medicine together can increase how much both affect your body. For example, one drink with a cold medicine could affect you as much as several drinks alone would.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a four-way intersection is coming.

questions.question: Changing from one lane to another is best done:

options.text: When a car is in your blind spot.

questions.explanation: Always change lanes gradually and carefully. Only change lanes when you need to. Every lane change increases the chance of an accident.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead curves and winds.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. You should:

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians on or crossing the road. Be extra careful where children are present. Always let pedestrians cross in a crosswalk.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing with no warning signals (such as flashing lights or gates), a driver should slow down, look, and listen.
questions.explanation: If a railroad crossing has no warning devices or only a crossbuck sign, slow down. Look both ways and listen for a train. Only cross the tracks when it is safe.

questions.question: If a traffic signal light is green and a police officer signals for you to stop, you should:

options.text: Do what the vehicle in front of you does.

questions.explanation: You must obey a police officer's instructions, even if they conflict with traffic signals or signs.

questions.question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:
questions.explanation: When you see an aggressive driver, the safest thing to do is get out of their way. Never try to compete with other drivers.

questions.question: Worn or bald tires:
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance and make turning harder. Tires without good tread also make hydroplaning more likely.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: Before you enter an intersection, look to your:
questions.explanation: Before entering an intersection, look left and right for vehicles and pedestrians. Look left a second time because vehicles from your left will be closer than those from your right. Check across the entire intersection before moving to make sure it is clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must go straight ahead.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road joins from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is ahead. A road joins from the right.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect you?

options.text: It gives you a false sense of confidence.

questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. It slows your reaction time, coordination, and balance. Alcohol also harms your vision and ability to judge distance, making it harder to react to what's happening around you.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol or other drugs from your system?
questions.explanation: Alcohol enters your system quickly but leaves slowly. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not reduce blood alcohol content. Only time will lower it.

questions.question: When getting your driver license, you may:

options.text: Choose to become an organ and tissue donor.

questions.explanation: If you are 18 or older, you can become an organ and tissue donor when getting your driver license. If you are a male between 18 and 25, the DMV will register you with Selective Service unless you opt out. If you are a U.S. citizen who will be 18 by the next election, you can register to vote or update your registration.
